model_interpretation.claim: Portable 8-byte SWAR masks may reduce per-byte control flow on mixed-width inputs by classifying byte lanes, shifting lead masks into expected continuation positions, checking restricted second-byte ranges, and carrying boundary state. The lane-mask and carry bookkeeping may instead cost more than the scalar control, so this is a hypothesis to measure, not a claimed speedup.

model_interpretation.claim: A safer hybrid may retain the throughput benefit of portable 8-byte bit-mask validation for complete blocks while avoiding fragile carried boundary state: when a block may end inside a code point, validate that block and the remaining suffix with the supplied scalar control. items.subject: Whole-stream SIMD UTF-8 validation with cross-block state
items.objective: Primary hypothesis: SIMD masks validate UTF-8 constraints across the whole buffer, unlike T2's ASCII-span locator. Explore block classification, shifted continuation requirements, restricted second-byte checks, cross-block state, and a bounded tail. Compare relevant SIMD variants only when supported by the frozen target and unchanged build; do not alter flags or add runtime environment probing. Keep the supplied scalar implementation as a control, and report any useful hybrid as a distinct variant rather than excluding it. Preserve exact scalar-value validation, ABI, output, and thread budget. Use the official mixed-width n=65536 timing for performance and official ASCII/malformed checks for correctness, paying particular attention to vector boundaries and truncations where covered. Record failed variants.
